title: シナノキの六月
subject: an urban beekeeper who keeps hives on the roof of a Ginza department store, lifting the frames at noon above the lunchtime crowds and tasting the honey turn minty when the street's linden trees flower in June
caption: Japanese bossa nova in the soft Brazilian-inspired style of Tokyo bossa nova singers. Nylon-string guitar playing the classic bossa batida with major-seventh and ninth chords; brushes swept on the snare with a quiet cross-stick rim click; upright bass on soft two-feel roots and fifths; an alto flute answering the vocal lines; light Rhodes electric piano comping in the chorus. Intimate close-mic acoustic recording, low volume, warm small room, almost no reverb. Female voice, breathy and soft in a low-mid register, sung almost at speaking volume. 128 BPM, F major. Gentle, wry and unhurried. No pop drums, no synth pads, no autotune, no string swells, no samba percussion section.
lyrics:
[Intro - nylon-string guitar batida and brushed snare]

[Verse 1]
昼の十二時 デパートの屋上
「関係者以外」の 扉の向こう
面布をかぶって ふたを開けると
巣枠いっぱいに 蜂が歩く

[Chorus]
下の通りは お昼休み
ランチの列が 角まで続く
巣箱に煙を ふわりとかけて
一枚ずつ 枠を上げる

[Verse 2]
六月になって 通りのシナノキ
小さな花が 咲きはじめた
指ですくった 蜜をなめると
先週よりも すっとして甘い

[Chorus]
下の通りは お昼休み
誰も見上げや しないけど
今日の蜜には シナノキの花
銀座の六月を 舌にのせる

[Bridge - alto flute and Rhodes]
四丁目の信号を 人は待つ
蜂は待たずに まっすぐ渡る

[Outro - guitar alone, slowing]
来週は どんな味がするかな
